data.title: UBS mulls shifting some job roles from Europe to India in next couple of years - report
data.description:
UBS Group is planning to shift certain job roles from Europe to India over the next couple of years, Bloomberg News reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

The push is part of a long-term strategy plan to reduce costs and simplify operations, the report published on Thursday noted.

A vast majority of the roles are currently held in Poland, according to one of the sources.

The job roles that are set to be affected are junior- to mid-level, while some more senior roles will be hired out of India in the future, Bloomberg reported.

The depreciation of the Indian currency is said to be one of the key attractions for global banks.

data.title: Sugar futures sink as funds liquidate long positions
data.description:
Sugar futures on ICE fell sharply on Thursday, with New York raw sugar prices losing nearly 5%, as funds liquidated a large part of their long positions to pocket profits before end-of-year books' squaring.

Robusta coffee, meanwhile, fell to a fresh 2-1/2 year low.

SUGAR

* Raw sugar settled down 0.88 cent, or 4.9%, at 17.16 cents per lb after setting a near two-month low of 17.13 cents.

* Dealers said funds have been scaling back a net long position in raw sugar with the market looking technically bearish after breaking below key support levels.

* "We had that 18 cent support level for a while, and when it broke I think several (sell) stops were triggered," said Murilo Barros de Mello, trading director at Hedgepoint Global Markets.

* He believes financial investors decided to pocket gains before the end of the year, but thinks the liquidation is mostly done as fundamentals are not bearish, in general, with production problems in several countries.

* On news, Pakistan's state trading agency TCP is believed to have sold about 96,000 metric tons of white sugar in an international tender seeking to sell and export up to 108,000 tons, which closed last week.

* White sugar lost 3.7% to $488.20 a metric ton.

COFFEE

* Robusta coffee settled down $41, or 1.4%, at $2,978 a ton after setting a 2-1/2 year low of $2,945.

* Dealers said the flow of newly harvested robusta beans from Vietnam had contributed to the recent decline in prices while the recent weakness of Brazil's real had encouraged exports from the world's top coffee producer.

* "Expectations of increased global supplies are weighing on prices with the Vietnam harvest underway and the weak Brazilian real encouraging exports," said a trader based in Vietnam.

* Brazil's currency fell to its lowest level since April 2025 on Thursday.

* Arabica coffee rose 0.2% to $2.76 per lb.

* Colombia coffee production is expected to rebound in the new season, said the USDA on Thursday.

COCOA

* London cocoa ​​settled up £145, or 3.7%, at £4,036 per ton.

* Dealers said low port arrivals in top grower Ivory Coast had helped to underpin the market with the El Niño weather event set to curb global production in the 2026/27 season.

* Ecuador exports could fall by as much as 10% in 2027 because of heavy rains linked to the El Niño, the head of the country's cocoa exporters' association said on Thursday.

* Ample availability of cocoa from the 2025/26 crop, however, continued to keep a lid on prices with exchange stocks well above year-ago levels.

* New York cocoa gained 4% to $5,201 a ton.

data.title: Treasuries Move Modestly Higher After Recovering From Initial Pullback
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - Treasuries gave back ground in early trading on Thursday but have shown a notable turnaround over the course of the session.

Bond prices have climbed well off their worst levels of the day and into positive territory. As a result, the yield on the benchmark ten-year note, which moves opposite of its price, has dipped 1.8 basis points to 5.048 percent.

With the downturn, the ten-year yield has moved lower for the fourth straight day, pulling back further off its highest levels in a month.

The strength that emerged among treasuries may have reflected bonds' appeal as a safe haven as selling pressure intensified on Wall Street.

After turning in a mixed performance early in the day, stocks showed a significant move to the downside soon after intelligence company Anthropic (ANT) made its debut on the Nasdaq.

While the Claude developer priced its initial public offering at a higher-than-expected $83 per share and soared by nearly 40 percent as it began trading, the stock has pulled back well off its highs since then.

The pullback by Anthropic and the subsequent sell-off on Wall Street has partly been attributed to profit taking amid lingering concerns about where the AI trade goes from here.

In U.S. economic news, the Labor Department released a report showing first-time claims for U.S. unemployment benefits unexpectedly edged slightly higher in the week ended November 14th.

The report said initial jobless claims inched up to 203,000, an increase of 1,000 from the previous week's revised level of 202,000.

Economists had expected jobless claims to slip to 198,000 from the 200,000 originally reported for the previous week.

With the unexpected uptick, jobless claims reached their highest level since hitting 207,000 in the week ended September 5th.

data.title: U.S. data center count dwarfs the rest of the world combined
data.description:
The United States now accounts for 5,044 data centers as of October 2026, more than eight times the 595 facilities in the United Kingdom, the next-highest total worldwide.

The gap is even wider in aggregate: the combined data center counts of the following nine countries still fall short of the U.S. figure alone.

This concentration of capacity is drawing fresh scrutiny on the day Anthropic completes its public listing, an event that has focused attention on the artificial intelligence sector and the physical infrastructure required to train and run large models. Germany ranks third with 580 centers, followed by China (443), France (401), India (338), Australia (337), Canada (299), Italy (273), and Japan (269).

Compiled from Data Center Map via Statista and visualized by Arbor Data Science, the rankings highlight the United States as the clear epicenter of digital infrastructure.

As AI systems become more compute-intensive, the geographic skew positions American facilities at the center of model development and deployment. The same concentration also intensifies questions around power demand, cooling requirements, and the competitive landscape as other nations seek to expand their own capacity.

data.title: Wheat, Corn Futures Pick Up After Selloff — Daily Grain Highlights
data.description:
By Anthony Harrup

  • Wheat for December delivery rose 1.4% Thursday on the Chicago Board of Trade to $5.78 1/4 a bushel as grains picked up from the previous day's commodity selloff.
  • Corn for December delivery rose 0.8% to $4.39 a bushel.
  • Soybeans for January delivery fell 0.8% to $12.07 1/2 a bushel.

HIGHLIGHTS

Weak Bounce: Wheat and corn futures picked up some of the previous day's lost ground when commodities sold off broadly. Soybeans were the most resilient in the selloff and slipped a bit further Thursday.

"A range-bound trade is possible for the beans as the market monitors South American weather," Doug Bergman of RCM Alternatives said in a note. "South American crop prospects look good, but there is a lot of growing season left."

Killjoy Currency: The U.S. dollar's rise to a near 20-month high is putting pressure on commodities broadly, including grains.

"The dollar has softened slightly, allowing an overnight rally, however the dollar is again showing a little strength into the mid-session which is pulling values off their highs," said Brian Hoops, president of Midwest Market Solutions.

Good early season growing conditions in South America and the stronger dollar have kept the grains in a solid downtrend, he said. "Until the technical trend changes or the dollar tops out, rallies will prove difficult to sustain."

Export Sales: Wheat sales for the 2026-27 marketing year were 344,800 metric tons in the week ended Nov. 12, up 89% from the week before, the USDA said. Soybean sales for 2026-27 rose 30% to 1.5 million tons, while corn sales fell 45% to 1.59 million tons. An additional 41,900 tons of corn were sold for the 2027-28 marketing year.

Flash Sale: The USDA reported a sale of 200,844 metric tons of soybeans for delivery to Mexico during the 2026-2027 marketing year.

INSIGHT

Going Abroad: The U.S. Agriculture Department plans trade missions to six countries in 2027, from Venezuela to South Korea, seeking improved access to global markets for U.S. producers. The 10 agribusiness trade missions held since January 2025 generated $154 million in 12-month projected sales, the USDA said.

"These results translate into better market access and increased sales for American farmers, ranchers, and producers," the USDA said. Other countries on the roster for next year are Costa Rica, Ecuador, Poland and Thailand.

On the Bright Side: U.S. corn exports are running below their year-ago levels but could get a boost, along with prices, from Europe's shortfall and Ukraine's inability to ship grains in 2026, analysts at Rabobank said in a report.

EU production was down by almost 10 million metric tons this year due to drought, and while estimates show imports up by just 2 million or 3 million tons, that could change, they said. Given damage to Ukrainian export infrastructure, "importers may be left scrambling for corn in the next year if Ukraine can't ship."

AHEAD

  • The USDA is scheduled to release its monthly Cattle on Feed Report at 3 p.m. EST Friday.
  • The USDA is due to release its weekly Grain Export Inspections Report at 11 a.m. EST Monday.
  • The USDA is scheduled to release its weekly Crop Progress Report at 4 p.m. EST Monday.

data.title: Health Rounds: GLP-1 drugs tied to heart improvements in patients with obesity and heart failure
data.description:
By Nancy Lapid

Hello Health Rounds readers! The benefits of widely used GLP-1 medications beyond weight loss continue to pile up as evidenced by a series of studies we cover today that were presented at the Obesity Week 2026 medical meeting in Washington.

GLP-1 drugs may strengthen failing hearts

Use of GLP-1 drugs by patients with obesity and heart failure was associated with significant heart muscle improvements, according to a study by Mayo Clinic researchers presented at the obesity meeting.

Everyone in the study had heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, meaning the heart's left ventricle was only weakly pushing blood out toward the body.

After one year, those taking GLP-1 medications showed significantly greater improvements in left ventricular size, shape, structure, and function than a closely matched control group of patients with obesity, researchers reported.

Those on GLP-1 therapy were taking either semaglutide, sold by Novo Nordisk as Wegovy and Ozempic, or tirzepatide, sold by Eli Lilly as Zepbound and Mounjaro.

Not surprisingly, the 146 patients in the GLP-1 group had significantly greater total body-weight loss than the 237 who were not taking the medicines.

The study was only designed to analyze changes at one year, but so-called “exploratory two-year analyses” — intended to generate new hypotheses for future studies — showed continued improvements in left ventricular ejection fraction and heart size, the researchers said.

Most of the improvements remained significant even after accounting for weight changes, suggesting that some of the positive effects were due to the drugs themselves rather than weight reduction, the researchers also reported.

A week earlier at the American Heart Association's Scientific Sessions in Chicago, a separate team of Mayo Clinic researchers reported on 81 adults with obesity and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction — that is, the left ventricle wasn’t particularly weak — who received semaglutide or a placebo for 52 weeks.

Treatment with semaglutide improved pressures inside the heart during exercise and at rest and was associated with remission of heart failure in more than half of treated patients, the researchers reported in Nature Medicine.

Zepbound can be cost-saving, Eli Lilly says

Eli Lilly’s expensive obesity drug Zepbound is ultimately cost-saving over time, according to data presented by the Indianapolis-based drugmaker.

Researchers compared trends in healthcare costs and utilization among more than 171,000 adults treated for at least a year with Zepbound for weight management, and the same number of similar but untreated individuals. No one in the study had diabetes.

During follow-up, healthcare costs remained stable in the Zepbound group but rose steadily in the control group. In one analysis, healthcare costs per month in patients not receiving Zepbound grew by an estimated $29 at 3-6 months, $82 at 6-12 months, and $120 at 12-18 months.

Zepbound-treated patients had 7% fewer hospitalizations and emergency department visits at 3-6 months. That climbed to 18% fewer for up to 12 months and a 34% reduction at 12-18 months.

“These findings suggest that beyond its clinical benefits, tirzepatide may deliver growing economic value over time,” Lilly’s researchers concluded in a brief summary of their presentation known as an abstract.

They did not report on what patients had paid for the medication or whether the savings completely offset the costs.

Zepbound can cost more than $1,000 per month without insurance. A recent study by CVS Health said employers and other health plan sponsors could break even on GLP-1 drugs if they are priced below $350 per month, as reduced use of medical services lowers spending enough to offset drug costs.

A separate study presented at the obesity meeting suggests GLP-1 use is associated with improved labor market outcomes.

Using data from a nationally representative internet panel of approximately 15,000 US adults, researchers found improvements in labor-force participation and ongoing improvements in productivity, following initiation of the drugs.

The results are relevant for employers considering coverage decisions, the researchers said, as many companies have dropped coverage of the medications due to overall costs.

“If GLP-1s improve worker productivity and participation, expanded access may yield returns in the form of higher output and reduced absenteeism,” they said.

GLP-1 use by seniors linked with fewer falls

Among older adults with obesity, GLP-1 use was associated with lower risks of falls and wheelchair dependence, according to a two-year study that tracked more than 122,000 patients age 65 and older without impaired mobility.

In these patients who were taking GLP-1 drugs or the common diabetes medication metformin, GLP-1 use was associated with a 13% lower risk of falls and a 37% lower risk of new-onset wheelchair dependence, the researchers reported.

The study did not compare patterns of weight loss, and it cannot prove the GLP-1 drugs prevented falls and wheelchair dependence.

Still, the researchers say, the findings suggest a potential role for the drugs in preserving independence among older adults with obesity, with implications for quality of life and healthcare utilization.

In April 2022, Anthropic announced a $580M funding round led by Bankman-Fried, who was then one of the most influential figures in the crypto industry.

Following the stunning collapse of FTX, its bankruptcy estate was forced to sell the Anthropic stake for about $1.3B in 2024 to help repay creditors.

That stake would be worth a whopping $37B at Anthropic's $83-a-share IPO price—a debut that minted a new class of millionaires among at least 4,250 employees and turned its seven co-founders into multibillionaires.

By Howard Schneider

The booming rollout of artificial intelligence technology could strain the US economy's capacity and further boost inflation that the Federal Reserve will have to counteract, Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said on Thursday, as AI firm Anthropic set a new record for an initial public offering of stock.

"The AI boom is contributing to the potential of overheating in the economy. I find it hard to ... look at that any other way," Goolsbee said in a conference call with reporters. "When you're getting major business investment, almost unprecedented levels of business investment, there's a high danger that the economy's capacity cannot handle that kind of a pig through the python."

data.title: Nvidia's stock falls further. It has lost $611 billion in six trading days.
data.description:
By Hannah Pedone

There are only 23 companies in the world with a market capitalization of $611 billion or higher

Shares of Nvidia fell again on Thursday.

Nvidia initially opened higher on Thursday, fueled in part by optimism surrounding Anthropic's IPO, but by midday the stock was back on track to clinch a six-day wipeout streak.

Shares of Nvidia (NVDA) were down 2.5% on Thursday afternoon. The company has lost $611 billion in market capitalization over the past six trading days. There are only 23 companies in the world with a market capitalization of $611 billion or higher, according to Dow Jones Market Data. Nvidia's stock was down 14.5% over this period.

"I don't think the losing streak is over yet," said Iskandar Rakhmatov, a portfolio manager at Zeus Quanto, a quant strategy research platform.

Rakhmatov told MarketWatch that a number of factors were working against the stock, one being that credit-ratings agency Moody's changed its outlook for Nvidia to stable from positive on Wednesday. A "positive" outlook indicates a higher likelihood that a company's credit rating could be upgraded in the medium term.

"That is not a rating downgrade, and nobody doubts Nvidia can pay its debts. But it puts the leadership gap in writing," he said.

Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia's longtime CEO after admitting to an affair with a woman associated with a Singapore company that has been a large customer of Nvidia's chips. Nvidia's board of directors has launched an indepdent investigation into whether Huang was the target of a foreign-intelligence operation. The board also appointed Nvidia's CFO, Colette Kress, to the position of interim CEO.

Rakhmatov said the uncertainty over the CEO position at Nvidia and the company's relationship with China are weighing on the stock. "Until there is a new CEO and the board's investigation ends, investors will apply a discount," he added.

Shay Boloor, chief market strategist at Futurum Equities, told MarketWatch that the market has seen some of the most "aggressive de-risking across growth and AI stocks in years," with Nvidia's stock falling nearly 30% despite the company delivering "exceptional" financial results for its last reported quarter as recently as Tuesday, while raising its outlook for the full year.

Yet Boloor said he's telling investors to "separate what's happening with Nvidia's stock from what's happening with Nvidia's business."

There's little evidence that demand for computing power is slowing, he said, noting that rental prices for graphics processing units are rising, among other factors.

"I still believe Nvidia is one of the most important companies in the AI economy, but that doesn't automatically make it a safe haven while those questions remain unanswered," he said.

Michael Casper, senior market strategist at HB Wealth, told MarketWatch that Nvidia's stock has seen a series of highs from November 2024 through January 2025 that "top out pretty much right at $150." Market technicians often look for "prior highs," especially ones that were "tested," meaning the price approaches the high and then breaks down.

Casper explained that traders "are likely lining up to buy" at $150. But if the price falls below that level, he said then there's "more downside to come as people holding at that level go underwater on their trade and attempt to cut losses," he explained.

Shares of Nvidia were changing hands for $147.26 on Thursday afternoon.

Sentara Capital founder Will Allen pointed out to MarketWatch that $148.80 was the "capitulation low" last Thursday morning when Huang announced his resignation. "That is an important level in the near term," he said.

-Hannah Pedone

This content was created by MarketWatch, which is operated by Dow Jones & Co. MarketWatch is published independently from Dow Jones Newswires and The Wall Street Journal.

data.title: US court ruling jeopardizes Sentinel Midstream's license for deepwater oil export project
data.description:
Key points:
  • Court says Texas GulfLink application area overlapped Enterprise's SPOT project area
  • Sentinel is working with MARAD to discuss its options for moving forward, source says
  • Sentinel cannot continue with the current license, source says
  • Company expects construction schedule to proceed as planned

By Arathy Somasekhar

A court ruling has jeopardized a license for Sentinel Midstream’s $2.1 billion deepwater crude oil export project off the Texas coast, an environmental group that petitioned the court said this week.

The ruling, which took effect on October 30, poses a setback and likely delays for the oil transportation and storage company, which has already started work on the project. It could also impact other pending deepwater port applications.

In August, a US appeals court voided a federal record of decision for Sentinel Midstream’s Texas GulfLink project, citing overlap with another deepwater project.

An official at Sentinel Midstream said work would continue on the project, characterizing it as "business as usual." But a source with knowledge of the situation said the company could not continue with the offshore project on the current license.

Last year, the US Maritime Administration (MARAD), in its record of decision (ROD), approved Texas GulfLink with conditions and the company received its license in January 2026. President Donald Trump has pushed for faster project approvals to bolster the US energy industry. Sentinel made a final investment decision in May and began construction.

MARAD's record of decision approving Texas GulfLink's application violated the Deepwater Port Act's requirement that only one deepwater port be approved per application area, the 5th US Circuit Court of Appeals said. Texas GulfLink's application area, when properly designated, would have intersected with Enterprise Products Partners' Sea Port Oil Terminal (SPOT) deepwater project.

Congress has struck a careful balance between promoting and regulating the construction and operation of deepwater ports, the court said, holding that the Deepwater Port Act requires an application area to encompass the entirety of a proposed deepwater port site, including any proposed pipeline.

“The Court’s decision is clear: it vacated the record of decision that was the foundation of GulfLink’s license. Now, MARAD has to revoke or suspend that license,” Michael Brown, a counsel for the petitioners, said on Wednesday.

Construction of the project cannot continue without a federal deepwater port license, said environmental group Better Brazoria Clean Air and Water in a press release this week.

MARAD said it was disappointed with the outcome and continues to pursue all avenues to achieve the President’s vision of American energy dominance.

"Sentinel is working with MARAD to discuss its options for moving forward. The company cannot continue with the current license," a source familiar with the matter said.

In comments to Reuters this week, Sentinel said its license has not been suspended or terminated.

Texas GulfLink, to be situated about 30 miles off Freeport, Texas, remains on track for a fourth-quarter 2028 operational date, Bruce Heine, a senior vice president at Sentinel, said this week, adding that given the narrow nature and scope of the issue, there are multiple paths to address the statutory concern without disrupting ongoing construction activities or overall project schedule.

"It remains business as usual for Texas GulfLink, with site development and improvement activities currently underway at our Jones Creek onshore terminal facility as we prepare to commence tank construction," Heine said, adding that major long-lead equipment and pipe have been purchased, and key construction contracts executed.

However, the company in its motion last month to stay the court mandate said that the Texas GulfLink’s license expressly incorporates the ROD as a compliance standard, adding that voiding the ROD in turn exposed the license to suspension or revocation by MARAD, and prevents construction of offshore components.

"At a minimum, the cloud on Texas GulfLink’s regulatory posture will harm Texas GulfLink in the marketplace," the company said then, adding that "given the uncertainty of its ROD and license, Texas GulfLink will not commence construction of the deepwater port under the current posture, even if the mandate is stayed."

Texas GulfLink plans to petition the Supreme Court, the company said in its motion. It added that there are two other pending deepwater ports under review with application areas similar to Texas GulfLink’s that will likely require redesignation as a result of the panel’s decision, potentially resulting in consequential impacts to those projects as well.

If Sentinel is required to resubmit its application, it would have to await a new ROD and license. While it took nearly seven years for Sentinel to secure approvals last time, MARAD has sped up its approval process under US President Donald Trump. It recently issued a deepwater project application license in just 410 days, nearly 3.7 years faster than ​the historical average.

The Texas GulfLink project aims to fully load a supertanker with about 2 million barrels of oil per day. The administration in recent weeks also approved deepwater port license applications for Energy Transfer's Blue Marlin Offshore Port, an oil export project off the Louisiana coast, and for ST LNG, which aims to ship liquefied natural gas off ​the Texas coast.

data.title: Mink Ventures Closes $521,298 In First Tranche of Non-Brokered Private Placement
data.description:
TORONTO, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Mink Ventures Corporation (“Mink” or the "Company") announces it has closed the first tranche of its non-brokered private placement (the “Offering”) announced on October 29, 2026. The Company has raised gross proceeds of $521,298 from the issuance of 1,188,100 hard dollar units (the "HD Units") at a price of $0.08 per HD Unit and the issuance of 4,059,524 CMETC eligible flow-through units (the “FT Units”) at a price of $0.105 per FT Unit in this first tranche. A second and final closing of the Offering is expected to occur on December 2, 2026.

Each HD Unit consists of one common share of the Company (a “Common Share”) and one Common Share purchase warrant (“HD Warrant”). Each HD Warrant shall entitle the holder thereof to acquire one (1) common share of the Company for a period of thirty-six (36) months from the date of issuance at an exercise price of $0.16.

Each FT Unit consists of one Common Share of the Company (a “FT Share”) and one Common Share purchase warrant (“FT Warrant”). Each FT Warrant shall entitle the holder thereof to acquire one (1) common share of the Company for a period of thirty-six (36) months from the date of issuance at an exercise price of $0.16.

The FT Shares were issued as “flow-through shares” within the meaning of the Income Tax Act (Canada) (the “Tax Act”). An amount equal to the portion of the subscription price that is directly attributable to the consideration paid for the subscription and issuance of the FT Shares will be used to incur eligible resource exploration expenses which will qualify as (i) “Canadian exploration expenses” (as defined in the Tax Act), and (ii) “flow-through critical mineral mining expenditures” (as defined in subsection 127(9) of the Tax Act) (collectively, the “Qualifying Expenditures”). Qualifying Expenditures in an aggregate amount equal to the gross proceeds raised from the issuance of the FT Shares will be renounced to the initial purchasers of the FT Units with an effective date no later than December 31, 2026. The FT Warrants were not issued as “flow-through shares” within the meaning of the Tax Act.

All securities issued in the closing of this tranche of the Offering are subject to statutory four month plus a day hold periods expiring on March 20, 2027. The Offering is subject to obtaining final approval of the TSX Venture Exchange.

Certain directors and officers of the Company purchased an aggregate of 63,100 HD Units pursuant to the Offering, constituting a “related party transaction” as such term is defined by Multilateral Instrument 61-101 - Protection of Minority Security Holders in Special Transactions (“MI 61-101”). The transaction will be exempt from the MI 61-101 valuation and minority approval requirements for related party transactions in connection with the Offering under sections 5.5(a) and 5.7(1)(a) of MI 61-101 as neither the fair market value (as determined under MI 61-101) of the subject matter of, nor the fair market value of the consideration for, the transaction, insofar as it involves the related party, exceeds 25% of the Company’s market capitalization (as determined under MI 61-101).

The Company paid aggregate cash finder’s fees totaling $40,020 and issued 398,761 in non-transferable finder's warrants (the "Finder's Warrants"). Each Finder's Warrant entitles the holder thereof to acquire one (1) common share of the Company for a period of thirty-six (36) months from the date of issuance at an exercise price of $0.16. All of the finder’s fees are subject to compliance with applicable securities legislation and TSX Venture Exchange policies.

The Company plans to use the net proceeds raised from the sale of the FT Units under the Offering for the exploration and advancement of the Company’s, Timmins area, critical minerals projects covering 115 km2, which include the Montcalm Ni Cu Co project, the Warren Cu Ni Co project, and the Rankin Cu Ni Co project; and, in respect of the HD Unit proceeds under the Offering, for general working capital purposes.

About Mink Ventures Corporation:

Mink Ventures Corporation is a Canadian mineral exploration company exploring for critical minerals in Ontario, Canada. It has a prospective, nickel copper cobalt exploration portfolio, with its Montcalm project, which now covers approximately 104 km2 adjacent to Glencore’s former Montcalm Mine with historical production of 3.93 million tonnes of ore grading 1.25% Ni, 0.67% Cu and 0.051% Co (Ontario Geological Survey, Atkinson, 2010), as well as its 11 km2 Warren Ni Cu Co Project and its newly optioned Rankin Cu Ni Co Property. These complementary nickel copper cobalt projects have excellent access and infrastructure and are in close proximity to the Timmins Mining Camp. The Company has 46,919,920 common shares outstanding after giving affect to this tranche of the Offering.

For further information about Mink Ventures Corporation please contact: Natasha Dixon, President & CEO, T: 250-882-5620 E: ndixon@minkventures.com or Kevin Filo, Director, T: 705-266-6818 or visit www.minkventures.com or www.sedarplus.ca

data.title: Dow drops below 50K for the first time in 5 months
data.description:
U.S. equities retreated sharply on Thursday afternoon, pushing the Dow Jones Industrial Average below 50,000 for the first time since mid-June and to its lowest level since May 5.

The blue-chip index fell roughly 2% on the session and now stands -10.3% below its all-time trading high of 54,744, reached back on August 5.

The decline leaves the Dow more than 5,000 points off that peak, reflecting a sustained pullback from the summer highs.

Moreover, the leg lower on the session was fueled by basically all the components within the Dow, with 29 of the 30 names in the red. The one green spot belonged to Chevron .

Spotlighted below are the top 10 worst Dow performers on Thursday:

  • Nike , -5.6%.
  • UnitedHealth Group , -5.1%.

data.title: ICE Review: Canola Swings Higher
data.description:
WINNIPEG, Manitoba--Partially recovering from Wednesday's pull back, Intercontinental Exchange canola futures reversed course on Thursday taking back a portion of the losses.

An analyst said he wasn't entirely sure as to what drove up canola Thursday, but noted it's "up one day, down the next" movement this week. The analyst suggested canola could see losses on Friday.

Although gains in crude oil turned softer on Thursday, there was still enough spillover to boost some of the vegetable oils, including canola. Additional support came from upticks in Chicago soyoil and European rapeseed.

Declines in Chicago soybeans and soymeal, plus those in Malaysian palm oil limited the upside in the Canadian oilseed.

The Canadian dollar was relatively steady on Thursday afternoon, with the loonie at 69.76 U.S. cents, compared to Wednesday's close of 69.80.

There were 63,520 canola contracts traded on Thursday, compared to 90,131 on Wednesday. Spreading accounted for 40,266 contracts traded.
